translationRepairs: Yuanjing was killed by Jinghe; Shilong, because he was far away, escaped.
Yuanjing was killed in the Jinghe era; Shilong, because he was far away, escaped.

s0011 元景爲景和所殺 uses the reign title 景和 as the era of the killing, not a personal agent; “killed by Jinghe” invents a person, while “killed in the Jinghe era” matches the Chinese and the idiomatic purge sense.
Their outer rampart is not strategically vital; clear it, and leave thirty paces from the inner wall—that is best.
Their outer rampart is not strategically vital; clear it, and leave thirty zhang from the inner metal wall—that is best.
s0122 使去金城三十丈 has the length unit 丈 and the fortified 金城; “thirty paces” and bare “inner wall” misrender both terms, which the proposal restores.
Ying had not yet sent pursuers, but the scattered soldiers feared Miao raids and gathered again—about twenty thousand—following Youzhi; when they were nearing Jiangling they then dispersed.
Ying had not yet sent pursuers, but the scattered soldiers feared Man raids and gathered again—about twenty thousand—following Youzhi; when they were nearing Jiangling they then dispersed.
s0097 畏蠻抄 refers to Man/southern tribal peoples generally, not the Miao; the proposal correctly drops Miao, but the slash form “Man/tribal” is awkward—plain “Man raids” fits the literal field.
Illness made him yield his post; he was offered Palace Attendant and Guardian General, declined, and was made Grand Master of the Palace Encampment instead, with Palace Attendant unchanged.
Illness made him yield his post; he was offered Palace Attendant and Guardian General, declined, and was made Left Household Grandee instead, with Palace Attendant unchanged.
s0150 轉左光祿大夫 is Left Household Grandee (光祿大夫); “Grand Master of the Palace Encampment” invents a different office the proposal correctly replaces.

Illness made him yield his post; he was reassigned Palace Attendant and Guardian General; he did not accept, and was moved to Grand Master of the Palace Encampment, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
Illness made him yield his post; he was reassigned Palace Attendant and Guardian General; he did not accept, and was moved to Left Household Grandee, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
The literal of s0150 likewise mistranslates 左光祿大夫; Left Household Grandee matches the title and the chapter’s later Household Grandee rendering.
Another edict read: "The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, bore virtue in his work and joined talent to the warp and woof of rule.
Another edict read: "The late Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, bore virtue in his work and joined talent to the warp and woof of rule.
s0153 故侍中 is Palace Attendant; Attendant-in-Ordinary is the standard English for 散騎常侍, not 侍中, so the proposal corrects a real office error.
Shilong was versed in number-craft; at Nitang he laid out a tomb and walked the ground with guests—nine visits in ten he would sit in the same place.
Shilong was versed in number-craft; at Nitang he laid out a tomb and walked the ground with guests—whether ten visits or five, he always sat in the same place.
s0166 十往五往 marks repeated visits, not a nine-in-ten ratio; the original invents that frequency, but “going ten times and five” is awkward—prefer “whether ten visits or five.”
Shilong was skilled in divination; at Nitang he opened a tomb and walked the site with guests—nine times in ten he would sit in the same spot.
Shilong was skilled in divination; at Nitang he opened a tomb and walked the site with guests—whether ten goings or five, he always sat in the same spot.
The literal’s “nine times in ten” invents a ratio absent from 十往五往; the proposal’s “ten goings and five goings” is still clumsy—revise to “whether ten goings or five.”

Gui left office as acting staff under the Grand Marshal of Prince Jiangxia, was assigned to outer military affairs, and with the headquarters became a Five Offices aide under the Grand Tutor—favored by Yigong.

Gui doffed plain clothes to serve as acting staff under the Grand Marshal of Prince Jiangxia, was assigned to outer military affairs, and with the headquarters became a Five Offices aide under the Grand Tutor—favored by Yigong.
s0176 解褐 marks first entry into office by doffing coarse cloth, not leaving office; “doffed plain clothes as” is still awkward—insert “to serve as” for clear English.
He rose to Crown Prince Attendant, Secretariat Director, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
He rose to Crown Prince Attendant, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant Gentleman of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
s0177 中書郎 is a Secretariat gentleman, not Director; 驃騎從事中郎 is Attendant Gentleman under the Fast Cavalry, not Attendant-in-Ordinary; 司徒 is Minister of Education, not 司空/Works.
He was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, Secretariat Director, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
He was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant Gentleman of the Fast Cavalry, and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
The literal of s0177 shares the same office mistranslations of 中書郎, 從事中郎, and 司徒; the proposed titles match the Chinese.
Another edict said: 「The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, upheld virtue in his station and united talent with statecraft.
Another edict said: 「The late Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, upheld virtue in his station and united talent with statecraft.
Literal s0153 likewise renders 侍中 as Attendant-in-Ordinary; Palace Attendant is the correct office title.
He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Palace Attendant as before.
s0159 侍中如故 continues the Palace Attendant title from the preceding edict; Attendant-in-Ordinary again confuses 侍中 with 散騎常侍.
He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Palace Attendant as before.
The literal of s0159 has the same 侍中如故 error; Palace Attendant as before is the accurate repair.
He was named General Who Exerts Might and Administrator of Donghai and Dongguan, but declined.
He was named Champion General and Administrator of Donghai and Dongguan, but declined.
s0189 冠軍將軍 is Champion General; “General Who Exerts Might” fits titles like 奮武將軍, not 冠軍.
He was appointed General Who Exerts Might and Administrator of the two commanderies Donghai and Dongguan, but did not accept,
He was appointed Champion General and Administrator of the two commanderies Donghai and Dongguan, but did not accept,
Literal s0189 repeats the 冠軍將軍 mistranslation; Champion General is correct.
In the second year he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat while keeping his commandant post.
In the second year he became Director of Capital Officials while keeping his commandant post.
s0193 都官尚書 is the capital-officials / justice Shangshu board, not the Imperial Secretariat as a whole; Director of Capital Officials restores the office.
In the second year he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat while keeping his commandant post.
In the second year he became Director of Capital Officials while keeping his commandant post.
The literal of s0193 shares the 都官尚書 error; the same Capital Officials rendering is warranted.

When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was General Who Exerts Might, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang's Northern Army, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; when the headquarters moved he became chief aide of the expeditionary force.

When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was Champion General, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang as Northern Palace Cadet, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; when the headquarters moved he became chief aide of the expeditionary force.
s0197 冠軍將軍 is Champion General, and 鄱陽王北中郎長史 is chief aide under the prince as Northern Palace Cadet (北中郎將), not “Northern Army.”
Once he took office he pleaded illness again and came back as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendor.
Once he took office he pleaded illness again and came back as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
s0203 還爲散騎常侍、光祿大夫 repeats the same offices as s0201; “Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry” and “Grand Master of Splendor” invent inconsistent titles.
On reaching his post he again pleaded illness and returned to serve as Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendor.
On reaching his post he again pleaded illness and returned to serve as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
Literal s0203 has the same invented office English; aligning with s0201’s Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness is correct.
In year 3 the righteous army came south; Dong Hun lent Gui his staff and set him to hold Shitou.
In year 3 the righteous army came south; the Marquis of Donghun lent Gui his staff and set him to hold Shitou.
s0222 東昏 is the epithet of the deposed emperor (東昏侯), not a two-syllable personal name “Dong Hun”; “the Marquis of Donghun” correctly identifies the ruler.

When the Shizu Emperor acceded, he was General Who Exerts Might, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang's Northern Army, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; he shifted with the headquarters to chief aide of the expeditionary force.

When the Shizu Emperor acceded, he was Champion General, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang as Northern Palace Cadet, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; he shifted with the headquarters to chief aide of the expeditionary force.
Literal s0197 needs the same fixes: 冠軍將軍 → Champion General; 北中郎長史 → aide to the Northern Palace Cadet, not Northern Army.
He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army, then was promoted to General Who Exerts Might and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army, then was promoted to Champion General and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
s0199 遷冠軍將軍 again is Champion General; “General Who Exerts Might” is the same false calque corrected elsewhere.
He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army; he was promoted to General Who Exerts Might and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army; he was promoted to Champion General and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
Literal s0199 likewise mistranslates 冠軍將軍; Champion General is the accurate title.
